question: The men's marathon best fell from 2 h 29 min in 1925 to 2 h 12 min by 1965. Where was it by 2025?
answer: At 2 h 0 min 35 s, set by Kelvin Kiptum in 2023. The twenty years to 1965 took off 15 minutes; the sixty since, only 11 more. Early gains come cheap; near the limits of lungs, legs and fuel, each minute costs more than the last. A steep stretch is a poor ruler.
move: Never extend the steepest stretch of a record; ask what limit it nears.
ask: Which of my improvements am I expecting to keep coming at their early pace?

verdict.under: Too fast. After 1965 the record slowed to a crawl: 2 h 0 min 35 s by 2025.
verdict.near: Right: the plunge did not last. Sixty years took off only another 11 minutes.
verdict.over: Lower than that: it kept falling, slowly, to 2 h 0 min 35 s in 2023.

source: IAAF, Progression of World Records, 2015; World Athletics
reference: IAAF, Progression of IAAF World Records, 2015 edition (marathon bests: Michelsen 2:29:01.8, 1925; Son 2:26:42, 1935; Shigematsu 2:12:00, 1965; Lopes 2:07:12, 1985; Tergat 2:04:55, 2003); World Athletics, men's marathon world record, Kiptum 2:00:35, Chicago, 2023
